'''Elżbieta Pleszczyńska''' (born 20 March 1933) is a Polish full [[professor]] of [[statistics]]<ref name="ipi">{{Cite web |url=http://gradestat.ipipan.waw.pl/english/tworcy.html#pleszczynska |title=The GRADESTAT program - authors |access-date=2008-08-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070701152737/http://gradestat.ipipan.waw.pl/english/tworcy.html#pleszczynska |archive-date=2007-07-01 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and an activist of [[disability rights movement]].<ref name="fund"/>

== Biography ==
She gained an M.Sc. in mathematics at [[University of Warsaw]], Faculty of Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry in 1956.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://b.leski.pl/ma|title=Mateczka|last=Leski|first=Krzysztof|date=2019-09-30|website=Leskipedia|access-date=2019-10-07|archive-date=2019-10-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191007142713/http://b.leski.pl/ma/|url-status=dead}}</ref> She held position at Institute of Mathematics [[Polish Academy of Sciences|PAS]] until 1972.<ref name="ipi"/> She received her Ph.D. in 1965 in the area of [[discriminant analysis]] ("Power of Test, and Separability of Hypothesis in Statistical Design of Experiments").<ref name="impan.gov.pl">{{cite web|url=https://www.impan.pl/pl/instytut/rada-naukowa/awanse/doktoraty|title=Doktoraty|website=Impan.pl|accessdate=13 December 2018|archive-date=5 March 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220305095335/https://www.impan.pl/pl/instytut/rada-naukowa/awanse/doktoraty|url-status=dead}}</ref> Her [[habilitation]] thesis, titled "Trend Estimation Problems in Time Series Analysis", was accepted in 1973.<ref name="impan.gov.pl"/>

From 1967 to 1968, she was a visiting researcher in [[University of Wales]] (Great Britain), and from 1971 to 1972, in [[University of Montreal]].<ref name="ipi"/> In 1973, she moved to the Institute of Computer Science, PAS. In 1977, 1979 and 1989, she was awarded by the Polish Academy of Sciences.<ref name="ipi"/> In 1981, she visited [[Italy]] invited by [[Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche|CNR]].<ref name="ipi"/> In the 1990s, she with her team started the so called [[grade data analysis]], a science of applying [[copula (statistics)|copula]] and rank methods to problems of [[correspondence analysis|correspondence]] and [[cluster analysis]] together with [[outlier]] detection.<ref>{{cite book|first=Teresa|last=Kowalczyk|author2=Elżbieta Pleszczyńska |author3=Fred Ruland |year=2004|title=Grade Models and Methods for Data Analysis with Applications for the Analysis of Data Populations|series=Studies in Fuzziness and Soft Computing|volume=151|publisher=Springer Verlag|location=Berlin Heidelberg New York}}</ref> The adjective ''grade'' here honors statisticians of the first half of the 20th century, who called [[cumulative distribution function]]s in this way.<ref>Example: {{cite book|first=Maurice G.|last=Kendall|authorlink=Maurice Kendall|title=Rank Correlation Methods|location=London|publisher=Charles Griffin & Company Limited|year=1948|pages=108–109}}</ref> In 1993, the [[President of the Republic of Poland]] [[Lech Wałęsa]] awarded Elżbieta Pleszczyńska with the Full Professor title in the area of mathematics.<ref name="ipi"/> In 2000, she was an invited consultant of the [[Cambridge University]].<ref name="ipi"/>

In the Institute of Computer Science PAS, she had been leader of the Statistical Data Analysis division for many years. According to the Polish law, professors in PAS must retire at the age of 70.<ref>[http://www.pan.pl/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=45&Itemid=246&limit=1&limitstart=7] {{dead link|date=December 2018}}</ref> Her retirement in 2003, although a bit confusing, did not stop her scientific and social activity.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ipipan.eu/recentpub/2004.html |title=Institute of Computer Science of the Polish Academy of Sciences |access-date=2008-08-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070518025859/http://www.ipipan.eu/recentpub/2004.html |archive-date=2007-05-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ipipan.eu/recentpub/2005.html |title=Institute of Computer Science of the Polish Academy of Sciences |access-date=2008-08-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720164131/http://www.ipipan.eu/recentpub/2005.html |archive-date=2011-07-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ipipan.eu/recentpub/2007.html |title=Institute of Computer Science of the Polish Academy of Sciences |access-date=2008-08-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720164209/http://www.ipipan.eu/recentpub/2007.html |archive-date=2011-07-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ipipan.eu/publishing/printer/pub2008pr.html |title=ICS PAS - Publishing Centre |access-date=2008-08-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720164221/http://www.ipipan.eu/publishing/printer/pub2008pr.html |archive-date=2011-07-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Scientific views ===
Prof. Pleszczyńska is known for her criticism of the classic statistical approach. Classic [[parametric statistics|parametric methods]], like [[Pearson correlation coefficient]], or [[least squares method]] produce comparable results only for comparable distribution types (in practice [[multivariate normal distribution]] is being assumed). Parametric [[statistical test]]s are derived from distribution assumptions. Classic methods fail if the input data contain strong [[outliers]], and interpretation of their results should be different for different distribution types. In practice, the underlying assumptions are often not checked, moreover they are always violated – there is no normal distribution in the real world, because every real variable is limited (for example people cannot be –170&nbsp;cm or +2&nbsp;km tall), and the normal distribution implies positive [[probability density function|probability density]] for every [[real number]]. In most cases the real distribution is [[skewness|skewed]] or [[discrete distribution|discrete]], which does not prevent people from using normal distribution methods. The extent of this violation can be measured, but its maximum accepted level is just a convention, not mathematics. The parametric methods always work out of their conditions of use. However, their results are often considered valid, which leads to "scientific" validation of false hypothesis. For the reasons mentioned above, Elżbieta Pleszczyńska is a strong advocate of [[explorative data analysis]]<ref>{{cite book|first=Janusz B.|last=Książyk|editor=Olaf Matyja |editor2=Elżbieta Pleszczyńska |editor3=Marek Wiech|title=Analiza danych medycznych i demograficznych przy użyciu programu GradeStat|place=Warszawa|year=2005|publisher=Instytut Podstaw Informatyki PAN, [[Children’s Memorial Health Institute|Centrum Zdrowia Dziecka]]|isbn=83-922508-0-X|pages=7 (preface by prof. Pleszczyńska)}}</ref> and [[non-parametric statistics]], like [[Spearman's rank correlation coefficient|Spearman's rho]], [[Kendall tau rank correlation coefficient|Kendall's tau]], or grade data analysis.

== Social work ==
Elżbieta Pleszczyńska has co-founded Foundation Supporting Physically Disabled Mathematicians and Computer Specialists in [[Warsaw]] (September 1990).<ref name="fund">{{Cite web |url=http://www.idn.org.pl/fpmiinr_en/ |title=The Foundation for Helping Physically Disabled Mathematicians and Computer Scientists |access-date=2008-08-09 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121221220611/http://www.idn.org.pl/fpmiinr_en/ |archive-date=2012-12-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://idn.org.pl/fpmiinr/doeuropy5/czesc2.htm|title=Internetowa wersja preprintu|website=Idn.org.pl|accessdate=13 December 2018}}</ref> She has been the Foundation chairman for multiple years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cs.put.poznan.pl/archiwumpti/download/Biuletyny/199103.pdf|title=Wyniki konkursu prac magisterskich|website=Cs.put.poznan.pl|accessdate=13 December 2018}}</ref><ref name="do Europy 4">{{cite web|url=http://idn.org.pl/fpmiinr/doeuropy4/brosz2000_3.htm|title=Fundacja w 1999 roku|website=Idn.org.pl|accessdate=13 December 2018}}</ref><ref name="do Europy 6">{{cite web|url=http://idn.org.pl/fpmiinr/doeuropy6/art70.html|title=Na wozku inwalidzkim po Infostradzie do Europy? cz. VI|website=Idn.org.pl|accessdate=13 December 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://fpmiinr.idn.org.pl/rada.html |title=Archived copy |access-date=2008-08-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210135531/http://fpmiinr.idn.org.pl/rada.html |archive-date=2009-02-10 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

The Foundation under her leadership was mainly interested in the professional advancement of physically disabled people via technology and [[remote work]].<ref name="fund"/><ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.niepelnosprawni.pl/ledge/x/11055;jsessionid=A3CC9DDA959B8B7E74246916DB7C9EEE |title=Działalność Fundacji Aktywizacja |website=Niepelnosprawni.pl}}</ref>

Pleszczyńska has been continuously focusing attention of the public opinion on rights of disable people, in her periodical reports.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.idn.org.pl/fpmiinr/publikacje.html |title=Archived copy |access-date=2008-08-09 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081202183807/http://www.idn.org.pl/fpmiinr/publikacje.html |archive-date=2008-12-02 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Private life ==
She had a son, {{ill|Krzysztof Leski|pl|Krzysztof_Leski}}, who was a journalist. Pieszczyńska also had two grandchildren. She lived in Warsaw [[Wola]] district. Since July 2019, she was in elderly care.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://b.leski.pl|title=Tylko Po Co|last=Leski|first=Krzysztof|date=|website=blog|access-date=2019-10-07|archive-date=2019-10-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191007141736/http://b.leski.pl/|url-status=dead}}</ref>
